signature: The USS Ace of Spades lying intact on a rocky valley floor 600 m down: three humming decks of berthing, mess, galley and dead controls, a reactor tunnel and an engine room under the bare hull, windows on both sides onto black water and fish, Kira's pirate drawings and post-its everywhere, and the Great Observer's eye at the glass.

exits.label: Escape hatch to Level 7
exits.source_quote: undo the escape hatch and swim out

entity_policy: SOURCED ONLY: the Great Observer as a scripted, harmless presence outside the hull (creaking and rocking currents, rhythmic tapping, its 20-inch eye pressed to the nearest window, one arm sweeping past, then it darts away; never damage). Pacific salmon, ragfish and Atka mackerel seen through the windows. The Crew (friendly residents) shown by their traces only. No hostile entities.
notes: SOURCE: sunken nuclear submarine USS Ace of Spades (SSN 744), Los Angeles-class layout plus windows on both sides; ~600 m deep in a rocky valley; controls dead, lights and kitchen appliances work, reactor runs; fridges with bottled water and food that restock; arrival in the berth or the canteen (leather couch, small metal tables, a few chairs); berth of empty mattresses; holds 140, crew of 20-100 asks non-residents to leave by the escape hatch; Kira's pirate drawings and signed post-it instructions; her undamaged note on the outside of the hull; Great Observer rocks, taps and watches; exit: undo the escape hatch at the top and swim out. ADAPTATION: hull compressed to 84 m (forward compartment 40 m on three decks, reactor compartment 14 m crossed by a tunnel at middle-deck height, engine room 30 m on two levels); exact room plan is ours after a generic Los Angeles-class arrangement; the arrival room is chosen by seed parity; the Crew is shown by traces (made-up racks, notice board, trade table, hand-written signs to the hatch) because no figure model is used; Great Observer cycle every 70-140 s (rocking push unless crouched, no damage); fridge restock after 40-75 s and heals 15; the outside note is read through the glass; Kira's post-it texts are ours in her voice. The outside of the boat is not walkable (page: unexplored); the ten-minute rule outside is therefore not modelled.
